title: BOOK TWO. On the end of man as citizen of God's kingdom — the absolutely highest and last end, or eternal beatitude. CHAPTER ONE. Whether there is some highest good of man, and that eternal, and what it is
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: together with the means by that same which he stands as directed to it — and the principles on that same which eternal salvation depends. the subject, that same is, man himself as a citizen belonging toward God; namely eternal beatitude; — the absolutely highest plus last end belonging toward man. The common part belonging toward sacred theology pursues three things: plus that same eternal, plus what it is — whether there stands as some highest good belonging toward man. CHAPTER ONE. as a citizen belonging toward God's kingdom — the absolutely highest plus last end, or eternal beatitude — on the end belonging toward man. BOOK TWO.
pass_b_english: BOOK TWO. On the end of man, as a citizen of God's kingdom — the absolutely highest and last end, or eternal beatitude.
CHAPTER ONE. Whether there is some highest good of man, and that eternal, and what it is.

The common part of sacred theology pursues three things: the absolutely highest and last end of man, namely eternal beatitude; the subject, that is, man himself as a citizen of God; and the principles on which eternal salvation depends, together with the means by which he is directed to it.
source_text: SACRAE THEOLOGIAE LIBER SECUNDUS, De fine hominis, ut civis regni Dei, absolute summo & ultimo seu aeterna beatitudine. CAPUT PRIMUM, An detur summum aliquod hominis bonum, idque aeternum & quid sit? Sacrae Theologiae pars communis tria persequitur, finem hominis absolute summum & ultimum, nempe beatitudinem aeternam, subjectum, puta hominem ipsum Dei civem, & principia a quibus dependet salus aeterna, cum mediis, quibus ad eam dirigitur.
